title: Twenty First Word First Station Third Warning Impatience And Three Kinds Of Patience

questions.question: In the Third Warning, what mistake does the nafs make about time and worship?
questions.answer: It mixes up the past, present, and future, and becomes upset by thinking about pains and duties that should not all be carried at once.

questions.question: What example is used to show this mistake?
questions.answer: A foolish army leader moves his soldiers to the sides at the wrong time and leaves the middle weak.

questions.question: What was the problem with sending troops to the left side?
questions.answer: There was no enemy there, so sending many soldiers there wasted strength.

questions.question: What happened because the center was left weak?
questions.answer: The enemy saw the opening, attacked the middle, and defeated him.

questions.question: According to the passage, what has happened to yesterday’s troubles now?
questions.answer: Their pain is gone, and what is left can become mercy, blessing, and reward.

questions.question: How should a person respond to past difficulties in worship?
questions.answer: The person should not get tired from remembering them, but should continue with fresh energy.

questions.question: Why is it foolish to become upset now about future worship or future disasters?
questions.answer: Those days have not come yet, so worrying about them now is like suffering before there is any real need.

questions.question: What comparison is given for worrying too early about future hardship?
questions.answer: It is like acting hungry or thirsty today because of hunger or thirst that may come later.

questions.question: What is the smart way to think about worship today?
questions.answer: A person should focus on today and see worship as a short, noble, and rewarding act with little hardship.

questions.question: What change can happen when a person thinks this way?
questions.answer: Sad, heavy feelings can turn into cheerful effort.

questions.question: What three kinds of patience are named in the passage?
questions.answer: Patience in worship, patience in staying away from sin, and patience during disasters.

questions.question: What should a person do with the patience Allah has given?
questions.answer: The person should use it in the right way and stay firm through hardships and troubles.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the Third Warning?
questions.answer: Do not waste strength on the past and future; use patience wisely and do today’s worship with courage and hope.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to in the Third Warning?
questions.answer: The impatient self, or nafs.

questions.question: Why does the passage call the nafs impatient?
questions.answer: Because it gets troubled by past pain and future worries instead of dealing wisely with the present.

questions.question: What kind of thinking is described as unreasonable at the start of the warning?
questions.answer: Feeling upset now by remembering old hardships and by imagining future duties and future sorrows.

questions.question: How does the military example help explain the nafs’s mistake?
questions.answer: It shows how strength is scattered in the wrong places instead of being kept where it is needed now.

questions.question: What good result remains from old hardships, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The painful part passes, but reward, blessing, and good meaning remain.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the future?
questions.answer: The future is not here yet, so a person should not carry its burdens before their time.

questions.question: How does the passage describe worrying today about tomorrow’s pain?
questions.answer: It describes it as senseless and foolish.

questions.question: What sentence should a reasonable person say about today’s worship?
questions.answer: The person should say that spending one hour on a beautiful and honored act with great reward and little burden is worthwhile.

questions.question: What feeling can replace discouragement if a person thinks correctly?
questions.answer: Sweet effort and willing energy can replace it.

questions.question: How many forms of patience does the passage mention?
questions.answer: Three.

questions.question: Which kind of patience helps a person avoid doing wrong?
questions.answer: Patience in keeping away from sin.

questions.question: Which kind of patience helps when hard events happen?
questions.answer: Patience in facing disasters.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen if patience is not wasted?
questions.answer: It will be enough, by Allah’s permission, to endure every hardship and trouble.

questions.question: What is the central advice given to the nafs in this passage?
questions.answer: Be patient, focus on the present, and do not let past pain or future fear stop worship.

questions.question: Why is the nafs compared to a foolish commander?
questions.answer: Because it uses its strength badly and leaves itself open to defeat.

questions.question: In the example, why was sending soldiers to the right side unnecessary?
questions.answer: Because that side was already no longer a threat.

questions.question: In the example, why was sending soldiers to the left side also unnecessary?
questions.answer: Because there was no enemy there at all.

questions.question: What does this teach about our thoughts and feelings?
questions.answer: We should not spend our emotional strength on things that are already over or not here yet.

questions.question: What has become of yesterday’s worship difficulties?
questions.answer: Their hardship has passed, while their benefit remains.

questions.question: How are old pains and struggles described after they pass?
questions.answer: They can become mercy, blessings, and reward.

questions.question: What should this understanding make a person do?
questions.answer: It should make the person continue worship with eagerness instead of boredom.

questions.question: Why is worrying about future worship compared to crying over future hunger?
questions.answer: Because both are about suffering now for something that has not happened yet.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the act of worship done today?
questions.answer: It is shown as pleasant, honorable, and highly rewarded.

questions.question: What are the three areas where patience is needed?
questions.answer: Worship, avoiding sins, and bearing disasters.

questions.question: What should a believer do with the strength of patience Allah gave?
questions.answer: Use it carefully and steadily instead of wasting it on wrong worries.

questions.question: What final encouragement is given at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Stay firm and keep going with the patience Allah has provided.

questions.question: What wrong habit of the nafs does the Third Warning try to correct?
questions.answer: The habit of becoming tired and upset by carrying the burdens of different times all at once.

questions.question: What two time periods does the nafs wrongly bring into the present?
questions.answer: The past and the future.

questions.question: What are the two kinds of past things mentioned that can upset a person?
questions.answer: Hard parts of worship and painful troubles.

questions.question: What are the two kinds of future things mentioned that can upset a person?
questions.answer: Future acts of worship and future disasters.

questions.question: Why is this kind of impatience not sensible?
questions.answer: Because a person is suffering from things that are either over already or have not happened yet.

questions.question: What picture from battle is used to explain this clearly?
questions.answer: A commander leaves the middle unprotected by sending forces where they are not needed.

questions.question: What lesson does the weak center teach us?
questions.answer: If we misuse our strength, we become weak where we most need help right now.

questions.question: What remains after yesterday’s pain is gone?
questions.answer: The good result, such as blessing and reward, remains.

questions.question: How should a person think about today’s worship instead?
questions.answer: As a short, worthwhile act of service that brings great reward.

questions.question: What happens to gloomy feelings when a person thinks in this healthy way?
questions.answer: They can turn into willing and hopeful effort.

questions.question: What is the first type of patience listed?
questions.answer: Patience in worship.

questions.question: What is the second type of patience listed?
questions.answer: Patience in staying away from sins.

questions.question: What is the third type of patience listed?
questions.answer: Patience during disasters and hardships.

questions.question: What promise is given about these forces of patience when used well?
questions.answer: They can be enough to face every hardship and disaster.

questions.question: In this passage, what is one major cause of impatience?
questions.answer: Thinking in the wrong way about time.

questions.question: How does wrong thinking about the past hurt a person?
questions.answer: It makes the person feel weighed down by pains that have already ended.

questions.question: How does wrong thinking about the future hurt a person?
questions.answer: It makes the person feel tired before future duties or trials even arrive.

questions.question: What story is used to show how harmful this is?
questions.answer: The story of a commander who badly arranges his army.

questions.question: Why was the commander’s plan foolish?
questions.answer: He used his forces where they were not needed and left the most important place undefended.

questions.question: What does the passage say happened to the pain of earlier troubles?
questions.answer: It disappeared.

questions.question: What stayed behind after those troubles passed?
questions.answer: Their good fruit, like mercy, blessing, and reward.

questions.question: What should a person feel when thinking of continuing worship?
questions.answer: Fresh eagerness and serious effort.

questions.question: Why is it called madness to be upset now about future burdens?
questions.answer: Because it is like acting as if a need already exists when it does not.

questions.question: How much of the day does the passage ask a person to think about giving to worship?
questions.answer: One hour.

questions.question: How is that hour of worship described?
questions.answer: It is described as beautiful, uplifting, and very rewarding, with only a little hardship.

questions.question: What three kinds of patience should a believer carry?
questions.answer: Patience in worship, patience against sin, and patience in calamity.

questions.question: What should a person avoid doing with the patience Allah gave?
questions.answer: The person should not waste it in the wrong way.

questions.question: If patience is used properly, what can it help a person do?
questions.answer: It can help the person endure difficulties and stand firm in hard times.

questions.question: What feeling in the nafs is directly addressed in the Third Warning?
questions.answer: Impatience.

questions.question: What does the passage say about being upset by both old troubles and future duties at the same time?
questions.answer: It says this is not wise.

questions.question: What kind of leader is used as an example in the warning?
questions.answer: A foolish military leader.

questions.question: What was wrong with the leader’s actions on the battlefield?
questions.answer: He sent strength to places that did not need it and left the center empty.

questions.question: What happened when the enemy noticed the center had no strength?
questions.answer: They attacked there and won.

questions.question: What lesson about the past is given after the battle example?
questions.answer: The hard part of yesterday is gone, and the lasting part can be mercy and reward.

questions.question: What should this teach a person about old struggles in worship?
questions.answer: They should not make the person lose heart now.

questions.question: What lesson about the future is given in the passage?
questions.answer: Since it has not come yet, a person should not suffer from it ahead of time.

questions.question: What everyday example shows how silly early worry is?
questions.answer: Feeling today’s hunger or thirst because of a later time.

questions.question: What should a reasonable person focus on when thinking about worship?
questions.answer: The person should focus on today only.

questions.question: How does the passage describe today’s act of worship?
questions.answer: As a pleasant and noble service with great reward and small burden.

questions.question: What can happen to bitterness and discouragement when a person thinks this way?
questions.answer: They can turn into a sweet desire to work and worship.

questions.question: Name the three kinds of patience taught here.
questions.answer: Patience in worship, patience in avoiding sin, and patience when disasters happen.

questions.question: What final instruction is given about these three kinds of patience?
questions.answer: Use the patience Allah gave, do not waste it, and stay strong through hardships.
